items.title: 61529_Maxine Sullivan oral history interview
items.q: as the smoke came out of the chimney, Sharkey Bonano played "The Saint Louis Blues".

ctx.x: the cabin had been standing there in a dilapidated condition, but the Housing Development had come through that area and a group of local citizens and of course with the help of the family, they decided that they were going to preserve the cabin. So it was torn down and they stored the logs around in different areas around, some in school yards, and they started out on a ten-year plan to re-structure the W. C. Handy house that he was born in, and also to set up a little W.C. Handy museum.

So I happened to be lucky enough to be down there when they dedicated the shirne. They had rebuilt the house with most of the original logs. Of course it's cement between the logs now. It's a two-room house and it's got a fire place and the old lamps they used in the early days. They have it converted to electrical fixtures, of course./ And the morning of the dedication they made a fire in the fire place and as the smoke came out of the chimney, Sharkey Bonano played "The Saint Louis Blues".
